premise: At 59, after 26 years as a home-health aide, I returned to care for my dying mother who left me 70% of her 1940s single-screen movie theater and projection-booth equipment worth $610,000, but my sister forged a codicil cutting me out and sold the property to a multiplex chain for $890,000, mailing me a $4,600 'concession' check. I found Mom’s original will inside a hollow carbon-arc film reel canister, voided the sale, and now run 'Flicker of Deceit Cinema,' where she threads projectors in a smock that says 'Spliced My Inheritance' and every ticket stub prints her probate-fraud docket.
